response.evidence: Denials occur across every race and sex group in the data (White, Asian, Hispanic or Latino, Black or African American, Other; Male, Female, Joint). Most groups are approved at high rates. The clearest pattern is financial, not demographic: applicants with debt-to-income ratios of >60% are denied in nearly every case regardless of race or sex, and denials are also concentrated in the 50%-60% DTI band. Black and 'Other' applicants show somewhat higher denial shares than the overall rate, but these groups are small, and many of their denials also have high DTI (50%-60% or >60%). That makes the difference statistically weak and largely explained by financial factors. Limitations: the data has no credit score, credit history, or employment information, and no stated denial reasons. It also contains nothing about your specific application. It therefore cannot rule out discrimination, nor can it confirm or rule out bias in your individual case.
